Container.Name: keystone-web
Container.Overview: Keystone Web — the browser frontend for the Keystone platform (Next.js, standalone). A backend-for-frontend: its own server holds the browser session (refresh token in an httpOnly cookie, access token in memory) and calls the keystone API container server-to-server; it never connects to the database. Stateless — no volumes. ONE neutral template for dev and prod: at creation set Name (keystone-web / keystone-web-dev), image tag (:stable / :dev), network mode / static IP, and KEYSTONE_API_URL pointing at the matching keystone API container (http://<api-ip>:8000). Put both containers behind the same public hostname on the reverse proxy: /v1/*, /docs and /openapi.json to the API, everything else to this container — and add this container's IP to the API's TRUSTED_PROXIES so per-IP auth throttling sees the browser rather than this container. Deploy check: GET /api/health reports release/sha plus API reachability.
Container.Description: Keystone Web — browser frontend (Next.js BFF) for the Keystone platform. Neutral template; set Name (keystone-web / keystone-web-dev), IP, image tag and KEYSTONE_API_URL at creation.

Config.Name: KEYSTONE_API_URL
Config.Description: Base URL of the keystone API container THIS instance talks to, e.g. http://<keystone-api-ip>:8000 (dev web -> dev API). Reached over the container network, never via the public hostname.

Config.Name: SESSION_COOKIE_MAX_AGE
Config.Description: Lifetime in seconds of the httpOnly refresh cookie. Keep equal to the API's refresh-token TTL (its JWT_REFRESH_TTL_SECONDS, default 43200 = 12 h): the API's session row is authoritative, so a longer value only leaves a dead cookie behind.
